newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WAPET eyes oil fields closures due to cyclone.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WAPET eyes oil fields closures due to cyclone.

text.p: A decision will be made early on Tuesday on whether to halt oil production at the Barrow Island and Thevenard oil fields as cyclone Rachel continues to cut a path down the Indian Ocean coast of Western Australia, West Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (WAPET) said on Monday.
Barrow Island continues to produce between 10,000 and 15,000 barrels a day, while output at Thevenard totals around 30,000 barrels a day, a WAPET spokesman told Reuters.
"We'll look at the situation on Tuesday morning," the spokesman said.
WAPET is a joint venture of Texaco Inc, Chevron Inc and Royal Dutch/Shell Group, each with two-sevenths stakes, and Mobil Corp, with one-seventh.

At 0700 GMT, cyclone Rachel was estimated to be 225 km west of the coastal community of Broome and 290 km northeast of Port Hedland, moving west southwest at 13 km an hour to the coast, the Bureau of Meteorology said.
The cyclone, currently rated at category two, with winds between 125 and 169 km an hour is expected to be upgraded to category three, meaning winds of up to 224 kmh, the bureau said.
Earlier on Monday Woodside Petroleum Ltd said it plans to halt production of crude oil at the Cossack Pioneer oil rig at around 1000 GMT (six p.m. local time) on Monday due to the cyclone.
The Cossack Pioneer pumps crude oil and gas from the Wanaea and Cossack fields on the North West Shelf.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf project are units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron, Royal Dutch/Shell and Woodside
Also on Monday, BHP said it was planning to halt crude production at the Griffin offshore oil field offshore Western Australia later on Monday due to the cyclone.
